newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German M3 money supply for December.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German M3 money supply for December.

text.p: Following are reactions from economists after the Bundesbank announced that M3 money supply grew 7.9 percent in December after expanding at a eight percent rate in November.
KEITH EDMONDS, CHIEF ANALYST, IBJ INTERNATIONAL IN LONDON:

I am slightly disappointed. I think the Bundesbank has a very good case to cut interest rates. In a month's time we are going to see very weak growth. We have seen weakness in industrial production. So I think the Bundesbank will want to edge the repo down.

M3 growth was very strong in first half of last year so as a result the January figure will come in at a very low figure. The Bundesbank will use that an exuse to cut interest rates. Bunds will be looking for further weak data. As a result of that the market will look towards an interest rate cut.

MICHEAL HOCHGUERTEL, BHF BANK, FRANKFURT: I don't think the figure is very significant. The question is where M3 will be at the start of next year and I'd expect a rather low figure due to statistical effects.

We could see a decrease below the corridor. January will be either within the corridor or below it. There is a chance that the repo rate will come down a little. I think it is safe to have long positions in the Bund market.
JUERGEN STANOWSKY, ECONOMIST, DRESDNER BANK, FRANKFURT:

January M3 will be at the lower end of the corridor. I don't think rates will come down. The total value of the D-mark has come down. This will boost exports. So I would not paint a Doomsday picture. I don't think there are domestic reasons for the Bundesbank to cut rates. Bunds will stay around where they are for now. --Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525
